does: Presses a clove of garlic flat under the blade of a knife, or under a pestle, and works it with salt into a damp, rough paste that melts into a dressing or a sauce.
how: Peel the clove and set it on a board with a little salt. The salt grips it and wears it down.
Lay the flat of a broad knife on the clove and press down with the heel of the hand until it splits.
Drag the blade over the pieces with the flat tilted, again and again, until the garlic is a damp paste with no lumps.
Scrape the paste into the dressing or the sauce and stir it in at once.

cues.text: The garlic turns from pieces to a pale, glossy, wet paste.
A sharp, raw scent rises as soon as it breaks, and fades into the dressing.

mistakes.mistake: Crushing without salt, so that the garlic slides about under the blade and stays in pieces.
mistakes.fix: Add a little salt first, so that it grips.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the paste on the board to turn bitter and harsh.
mistakes.fix: Stir it into the acid or the oil soon after it is done.

variant_of.differs: The garlic is pressed and dragged flat under a blade or a pestle for a few moments into a damp, rough paste, and not worked long in a mortar until it is smooth.
